Reference

Commands, options and results

Camera capture for people and agents: list, configure, capture and record cameras. For tasks step by step, read the guides; agents can read agents.md.

JSON results, exit codes and errors

Run any command with --json for one JSON document and a typed exit code.

--json (or CAPTUREFAB_JSON=1): one line on stdout, the result on exit 0, else {"error":{code,message,hint?,details?}}: code is the reason (see errors), the exit code its category. No nulls; warnings ≤10.

snake_case keys; units in names (exposure_us); times RFC 3339 UTC; lists bounded with truncated. Credentials: never printed; URLs are redacted.

capturefab schema COMMAND: arguments, result fields and errors. This page is generated from that output (contract version 1), so it lists exactly what the CLI accepts.

Exit codes
Exit codeCategory
0ok
1failed
2usage or input
3unavailable
4timeout
5unsupported
6storage full
130interrupted (143 SIGTERM, 129 SIGHUP)
Error codes in error.code
CodeExitMeaning
exists1the output exists (never overwritten); details.path
failed1the operation failed
feature_locked1another setting locks the feature now; see details.locked_by
incomplete1fewer results than requested; see details
camera_ambiguous2several cameras match; pick one of details.candidates with -c
feature_not_found2no such feature or control; see details.did_you_mean
invalid_choice2not one of details.choices
invalid_duration2not a valid duration (see grammars.duration)
not_writable2the feature is read-only
out_of_range2outside the feature's range; details {feature,value,min,max,inc,nearest,unit}
usage2invalid arguments or input
auth_rejected3the camera refused the sign-in
auth_required3the camera needs a sign-in; run login add
camera_busy3another process or job holds the camera; details.held_by when known
camera_not_found3no camera matches; details.candidates lists what answered
disconnected3the camera went away
ffmpeg_missing3FFmpeg could not be found or started
permission_denied3the OS refused access; see hint
session_not_found3no running session has that name
unavailable3the camera, stream or service cannot be reached
worker_crashed3the camera worker process died
frame_timeout4no frame arrived in time
timeout4the operation did not finish in time
trigger_timeout4a triggered camera got no trigger in time; details.trigger
unsupported5the camera or this build cannot do that
storage_full6disk full or below CAPTUREFAB_MIN_FREE; details {path,free_bytes?}
interrupted130stopped by a signal; details hold partial results

Global options, cameras and sessions

Options every command takes, how a camera is chosen and when a session is used.

--json, -q/--quiet, -v/--verbose, --session NAME (CAPTUREFAB_SESSION), --no-session (overrides it); before or after the command.

Global options
OptionMeaningEnvironment
--jsonOne JSON document on stdout: the result, or {"error":{...}} with a non-zero exitCAPTUREFAB_JSON
-q, --quietNo progress or notes on stderr; errors still print—
-v, --verboseMore detail on stderr, including camera worker logs—
--session NAMEUse this running session (session start or serve --name NAME)CAPTUREFAB_SESSION
--no-sessionNever use a running session: open the camera in a worker of this command—
-h, --helpPrint help (see more with '--help')—
-V, --versionPrint version—

-c/--camera CAM (CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA). Without it: the session's only camera, else the only camera list finds (not sim: or screens).

--session NAME, else a session holding the camera, else the auto session, open 60s after last use (--keep DUR); --keep 0 or --no-session: a worker of the command.

capture/record block until done; --background prints a job instead (jobs wait ID). Ctrl-C: capture exits 130 with details.files; open-ended record ends normally.

Selectors, names, durations and templates

The forms camera selectors, feature names, durations and output names take.

Value grammars
ValueForm
durationnumber+unit, repeatable: 500us, 250ms, 2s, 5m, 1h30m; 0; none where a wait may be unlimited. A bare number is invalid_duration
nameFeature | Feature[Selector=Value,…] | Feature[Value] (when one selector addresses it) | control: exposure, gain, fps, roi, format, trigger, auto_exposure, auto_wb
selectorlist id (gige:…, u3v:…, avfoundation:…, v4l2:…, dshow:…), serial, IPv4, rtsp(s)://, srt://, http(s)://, onvif://host[/path], file, sim:N[?drop=0..0.5&line0=every:DUR], sim:replay:PATH
template-o: {camera} {serial} {seq} {seq:N} {time} {date} {tag:KEY} {ext}; a folder holds {camera}-{time}-{seq}.{ext}; a taken name fails without {seq}, {time} or --on-exists number

Cameras and settings

Find a camera, read what it can do and change its settings.

capturefab list

List cameras: GigE Vision, USB3 Vision, webcams, ONVIF. Effect: read. Alias: ls.

capturefab list arguments
Argument or optionMeaningValues
--kind KINDOnly these kinds (comma-separated); screen captures and sim:0 are listed only when namedone of gige, u3v, webcam, onvif, screen, sim; repeatable
--timeout DURHow long GigE and ONVIF broadcasts collect answersdefault 1s
capturefab list
capturefab list --kind gige,u3v --timeout 3s
capturefab list --kind sim
capturefab --json list
capturefab list JSON result
FieldType and meaning
cameras[{id,kind:gige|u3v|webcam|screen|onvif|stream|file|sim,vendor,model,serial,address,held_by?:{session,idle_releases_in_s?}}] — pass id to -c; held_by: a session keeps it open, the auto session for idle_releases_in_s more seconds unless used
warnings[string] — transports that could not be searched

Errors: usage, failed, invalid_duration, timeout.

capturefab info

What a camera is and what it can do: size, format, exposure, gain, trigger, controls. Effect: read.

capturefab info arguments
Argument or optionMeaningValues
-c, --camera CAMCamera: list ID, serial, IP, rtsp://…, file path, sim:0[?drop=0.02&line0=every:500ms] (default: the only one)env CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA
--keep DURKeep the camera open in a session for this long after the command, so the next one starts at once (default 60s; 0 opens and closes it in this command alone)env CAPTUREFAB_KEEP
capturefab info -c sim:0
capturefab --json info -c gige:00c0df123456
capturefab info -c sim:0 --keep 5m
capturefab info JSON result

capturefab set

Change features or controls as one atomic change; a failure restores every value. Effect: camera_write.

capturefab set arguments
Argument or optionMeaningValues
-c, --camera CAMCamera: list ID, serial, IP, rtsp://…, file path, sim:0[?drop=0.02&line0=every:500ms] (default: the only one)env CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA
NAME=VALUE...NAME=VALUE: a feature (ExposureTime=10ms), a bank (TriggerMode[FrameStart]=On) or a control (exposure=5ms, roi=0,0,640,480)—
--dry-runCheck every value against the camera and show the writes in order; change nothing—
--keep DURKeep the camera open in a session for this long after the command, so the next one starts at once (default 60s; 0 opens and closes it in this command alone)env CAPTUREFAB_KEEP
capturefab set -c sim:0 exposure=5ms gain=3

capturefab set -c sim:0 'TriggerMode[FrameStart]=On' 'TriggerSource[FrameStart]=Line0'

capturefab set JSON result
FieldType and meaning
camerastring — camera ID
changed[{name,from,to}] — every value written, in order, to read back (may be rounded); autos turned off to unlock a value are listed too
dry_runtrue — with --dry-run
plan[{name,from,to}] — with --dry-run: the writes in order, none made
warnings[string] — with --dry-run: checks only the writes themselves can decide (a value another write of the change may unlock or bring into range)

Capture, record and measure

Save images and video, measure exposure and focus once or live, settle auto exposure.

capturefab capture

Save frames: one shot, a burst, a time lapse or a delayed capture; never overwrites. Effect: file_write.

capturefab capture arguments
Argument or optionMeaningValues
-c, --camera CAMCamera, repeatable: list ID, serial, IP, rtsp://…, file path, sim:0[?drop=0.02&line0=every:500ms] (default: the only one)env CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA; repeatable
-o, --output PATHFile, folder (existing, or ending in /) or template with {camera} {serial} {seq} {seq:N} {time} {date} {tag:KEY} {ext}; - writes one image to stdout (default: this folder, as {camera}-{time}-{seq}.png)—
-n, --count NFrames to save, 1..100000—
--every DURTime between frames of a time lapse, with -n or --for—
--for DURHow long a time lapse runs, with --every—
--at TIMEBegin at a time: HH:MM[:SS] here, or RFC 3339—
--in DURBegin after a delay—
-f, --format FORMATImage format when -o has no extension: png (default; 16-bit for Mono10..Mono16), jpg or raw (the exact bytes, with NAME.json beside)one of png, jpg, raw
--quality 1-100JPEG quality, 1..100 (default 90; without it, a Motion JPEG source's own JPEG is stored as it is)—
--set NAME=VALUEChange settings first, as one atomic change (as set does); repeatablerepeatable
--autoSettle exposure and gain first, then hold them (as auto does)—
--inspectMeasure the last frame as inspect does, and preview it: the result's inspect block—
--tag KEY=VALUETag the files: {tag:KEY} in -o, and in each image's metadata; repeatablerepeatable
--timeout DURHow long to wait for each frame (default: 5s, or 3 exposures and frame periods when longer); none waits for a trigger until stopped—
--fresh NFrames to let pass after the first one exposed after the last settings change, 0..10default 0
--warmup DURHow long a camera that sets its own exposure (a webcam, or ExposureAuto=Continuous; a network stream is already running) may take to settle after it starts; 0 takes frames at oncedefault 2s
--on-exists ON_EXISTSWhen a file name without {seq} exists: fail, or number (-0001, -0002, ...)one of fail, number; default fail
--manifest FILEAppend one JSON line per saved file (path, time, size, SHA-256, settings, tags) to this file—
--sync SYNCfile: each file reaches the disk before it is reported; none: skip that, for scratch capturesone of file, none; default file
--backgroundLeave the capture running in a session; print its job once it is armed or has saved its first frame (up to --timeout; with --timeout none, after 2s without waiting for a trigger)—
--progressReport progress on stderr, also without a terminal: a JSON line {progress:{job,camera,kind,state,saved,planned?,bytes?,elapsed_s,left_s?,next_s?}} as the job changes, at least each second—
--keep DURKeep the camera open in a session for this long after the command, so the next one starts at once (default 60s; 0 opens and closes it in this command alone)env CAPTUREFAB_KEEP
--dry-runShow the camera, files, settings and timing; capture nothing—
capturefab capture -c sim:0 -o shot.png
capturefab capture -c sim:0 -n 10 -o frames/
capturefab capture -c sim:0 --every 10s --for 1h -o 'lapse/{seq}.jpg' --background
capturefab capture -c sim:0 -o - > frame.png
capturefab capture JSON result
FieldType and meaning
after_changetrue — frames exposed before the camera's last settings change were let pass
autotrue — with --dry-run and --auto
bandwidth_mbpsfloat — with -c repeated, for GigE cameras that share a host network interface: the rate this one was paced to, its share of the interface (a warning when it could not be paced)
bit_depthint — bits per sample in the files: 16 for PNG of Mono10..Mono16 (samples at the top bits, sBIT says how many count), every bit for raw, else 8
bytesint — with -o -: the image's size
camerastring — camera ID
cameras[{camera,files,count,truncated?,width,height,pixel_format,bit_depth,source_bits?,settings,time,device_ts_ns?,frames,dropped,incomplete?,resent?,duration_s?,fps?,first_id?,last_id?,gaps?,consecutive?,after_change?,warmup_ms?,settled?,bandwidth_mbps?,warnings?,inspect?,dry_run?,output?,format?,every_s?,first_at?,ends_at?,auto?}] — with -c repeated: one result per camera; in error details, a failed camera's {camera,error,files?,truncated?,job?}
consecutivebool — a burst's frames follow one another with no frame missing
countint — frames saved
device_ts_nsint — the camera's clock when the first frame was taken (GigE, U3V, sim); never a date
droppedint — frames lost while it ran: the encoders' queue was full, or the transport lost them
dry_runtrue — with --dry-run; nothing was captured
duration_sfloat — first to last frame, for several
ends_atstring — with --dry-run, for a time lapse
every_sfloat — with --dry-run, for a time lapse
files[string] — absolute paths, in order; at most 1000, the rest counted in truncated
first_atstring — with --dry-run and --at/--in
first_idint — a burst's first frame's block ID
formatpng|jpg|raw — with --dry-run
fpsfloat — frames per second from the first frame to the last, by the camera's clock when it has one
framesint — frames the camera delivered while the capture ran, including those let pass
gapsint — block IDs missing between a burst's first and last frame
heightint
incompleteint — frames that arrived incomplete, where the transport counts them
inspect{exposure,verdict,suggest?,focus?,preview?} — with --inspect: the last frame measured as inspect measures it
job{id,camera,kind:capture|record|auto,state:armed|running|stopping|done|failed|cancelled|interrupted|lost,saved,planned?,bytes?,last_file?,next_at?,ends_at?,started,ended?,error?:{code,message}} — with --background, as jobs lists it, once armed or its first frame is saved
jobs[{id,camera,kind:capture|record|auto,state:armed|running|stopping|done|failed|cancelled|interrupted|lost,saved,planned?,bytes?,last_file?,next_at?,ends_at?,started,ended?,error?:{code,message}}] — with --background and -c repeated
last_idint — a burst's last frame's block ID
output"-" — with -o -: the image went to stdout
passthroughtrue — the JPEG files are the ones the source sent (an MJPEG webcam, stream or file), as they were, with the provenance comment: not decoded and encoded again
pixel_formatstring — the camera's PFNC format
resentint — packets the camera sent again, where the transport counts them
settings{exposure_us?,auto_exposure?,gain_db?,gain?,auto_gain?,auto_wb?,fps?,trigger?,black_level?,gamma?,binning?,offset_x?,offset_y?,reverse_x?,reverse_y?} — the camera's settings when the first frame was taken, as the camera has them; trigger: off, or its source (software, line0)
settledfalse — its exposure was still changing when --warmup ran out (with a warning)
skew_msint — with -c repeated: how far apart the cameras' first frames arrived; all were armed first and asked for a frame at the same moment
source_bitsint — the camera's bits per sample, when the files keep fewer (color or Bayer PNG, JPEG)
timestring — RFC 3339 time of the first frame
truncatedint — files saved but not listed
warmup_msint — how long a camera that sets its own exposure took to settle after it started
warnings[string]
widthint

capturefab record

Record video to a file or stream it to rtsp://, srt://, rtmp:// or udp://. Effect: file_write.

capturefab record arguments
Argument or optionMeaningValues
-c, --camera CAMCamera: list ID, serial, IP, rtsp://…, file path, sim:0[?drop=0.02&line0=every:500ms] (default: the only one)env CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA
-o, --output FILE|URLA file (.mkv, .mp4, .mov, .ts, .webm; it must not exist, or use {seq}) or a stream URL (rtsp://, srt://, rtmp://, udp://)required
--for DURStop after this long; without it, record until Ctrl-C (or jobs stop with --background)—
--fps NFrames per second written (default: the camera's frame rate); re-encodes a source that would be copied—
--codec CODECh264, hevc or av1 (where a hardware encoder has them), or ffv1 (lossless, .mkv). Default: an H.264 or HEVC stream, webcam or file is copied as it arrives, without re-encoding; anything else is encoded as h264one of h264, hevc, av1, ffv1
--bitrate RATETarget bitrate, such as 8M or 800k (default 8M; not for ffv1); re-encodes a source that would be copied—
--max-size SIZEEnd the recording, successfully, before the file outgrows this size, such as 2G—
--set NAME=VALUEChange settings first, as one atomic change (as set does); repeatablerepeatable
--autoSettle exposure and gain first, then hold them (as auto does)—
--timeout DURHow long to wait for the first frame; none waits for a trigger until stoppeddefault 10s
--warmup DURHow long a camera that sets its own exposure (a webcam, or ExposureAuto=Continuous; a network stream is already running) may take to settle before recording; 0 records at oncedefault 2s
--backgroundLeave the recording running in a session and print its job once the first frame is encoded—
--progressReport progress on stderr, also without a terminal: a JSON line {progress:{job,camera,kind,state,saved,planned?,bytes?,elapsed_s,left_s?,next_s?}} as the job changes, at least each second—
--keep DURKeep the camera open in a session for this long after the command, so the next one starts at once (default 60s; 0 opens and closes it in this command alone)env CAPTUREFAB_KEEP
capturefab record -c sim:0 -o clip.mp4 --for 30s
capturefab record -c sim:0 -o clip.mkv --codec ffv1 --for 5m
capturefab record -c sim:0 -o rtsp://localhost:8554/cam --background
capturefab record JSON result

capturefab inspect

Measure a fresh frame: exposure, clipping, focus, suggested exposure, a preview. Effect: read.

capturefab inspect arguments
Argument or optionMeaningValues
-c, --camera CAMCamera, repeatable: list ID, serial, IP, rtsp://…, file path, sim:0[?drop=0.02&line0=every:500ms] (default: the only one)env CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA; repeatable
--region X,Y,W,HMeasure only this part of the frame: X,Y,W,H as fractions 0..1—
--preview PATHWhere to write the preview (it must not exist), or none (default: a private folder doctor shows)—
--size PXThe preview's longest edge in pixels, 64..2048default 768
--fresh NFrames to let pass after the first one exposed after the last settings change, 0..10default 0
--timeout DURHow long to wait for the frame, up to 10m (default: 5s, or 3 exposures and frame periods when longer); none waits for a trigger until stopped—
--warmup DURHow long a camera that sets its own exposure (a webcam, or ExposureAuto=Continuous; a network stream is already running) may take to settle after it starts; 0 measures at oncedefault 2s
--set NAME=VALUEChange settings first, as one atomic change (as set does), then measure; repeatablerepeatable
--for DURMeasure a frame every --every for this long (at most 50 samples), as for focusing: the series, and the sharpest frame's measurements and preview—
--every DURTime between samples with --for (default 200ms)—
--clip-threshold SHAREShare of the measured pixels at full scale above which the verdict says clipped_high (default: any pixel with --region, else 0.005)—
--showDraw the preview in this terminal under the measurements (kitty, iTerm2, or colour blocks)—
--keep DURKeep the camera open in a session for this long after the command, so the next one starts at once (default 60s; 0 opens and closes it in this command alone)env CAPTUREFAB_KEEP
capturefab inspect -c sim:0
capturefab inspect -c sim:0 --set exposure=20ms --region 0.25,0.25,0.5,0.5
capturefab inspect -c sim:0 --keep 5m --preview none
capturefab inspect -c sim:0 --show

FieldType and meaning
after_changetrue — frames exposed before the camera's last settings change were let pass

camerastring — camera ID
cameras[{camera,frame,exposure?,verdict,suggest?,focus?,settings,preview?,after_change?,frames?,dropped?,incomplete?,resent?,warmup_ms?,settled?,warnings?,series?,best?,histogram?,channels?,region?,notes?}] — with -c repeated
channels{red,green,blue} — with -v, for color
droppedint — frames the transport lost meanwhile, where it counts them
exposure{mean,p1,p50,p99,clipped_low,clipped_high,clipped_low_px?,clipped_high_px?,max?} — brightness 0..1; shares and counts of pixels at black and at full scale, counted over every pixel of the region at the camera's bit depth; max: the brightest sample as a share of full scale
focus{sharpness} — variance of the Laplacian over the region; compare between frames of one camera and scene (-v adds tenengrad, brenner, variance)
frame{width,height,pixel_format,bits?,id?,device_ts_ns?,time,age_ms} — the frame measured, taken after the command began: its block ID and the camera's clock (ns, never a date) where the transport has them, and when it arrived
framesint — frames received for this inspection, the one measured included
histogram[16 ints] — with -v: luminance histogram
incompleteint — frames that arrived incomplete meanwhile, where the transport counts them
notes[string] — with -v
previewstring — the preview image's path; absent with --preview none
region{x,y,width,height,normalized} — with -v
resentint — packets the camera sent again meanwhile, where the transport counts them
series[{t,sharpness,mean}] — with --for: every sample, t in seconds from the first; the other fields describe the sharpest frame
settings{exposure_us?,gain_db?,gain?,fps?,pixel_format?} — in effect for the frame
settledfalse — its exposure was still changing when --warmup ran out (verdict not_settled, with a warning)
suggest{ev,exposure_us?,limited_by?:exposure_max|exposure_min|clipped} — how far to move exposure, in stops, toward mid-grey without clipping highlights; absent when close enough. clipped: most of the frame is clipped, so this is a first step; inspect again
verdict[ok|dark|bright|clipped_high|clipped_low|not_settled|not_measured]
warmup_msint — how long a camera that sets its own exposure took to settle after it started
warnings[string] — such as a camera still settling when --warmup ran out (verdict not_settled)

Presets

Save a camera's settings on this computer and restore them as one change.

capturefab preset

Saved camera settings (host-side, portable between cameras of a model).

A preset lives on this computer and can be applied to any camera of the model; a user set (exec 'UserSetSave[UserSet1]', or preset apply --persist) lives in the camera.

capturefab preset save bench -c sim:0
capturefab preset apply bench -c sim:0 --dry-run
capturefab preset list

capturefab preset apply

Restore a preset as one camera change; a failure puts every value back. Effect: camera_write.

capturefab preset apply arguments
Argument or optionMeaningValues
[NAME]—
-c, --camera CAMCamera: list ID, serial, IP, rtsp://…, file path, sim:0[?drop=0.02&line0=every:500ms] (default: the only one)env CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA
--file FILEApply a preset document from a file instead of a saved preset—
--dry-runShow what would change, disruptive changes included; change nothing—
--strictFail, changing nothing, if any saved value cannot be applied to this camera—
--allow-other-modelApply to a camera of another model; only settings both share change—
--persist USERSETThen save it in the camera's user set (default UserSet1) and make that the power-on default—
--keep DURKeep the camera open in a session for this long after the command, so the next one starts at once (default 60s; 0 opens and closes it in this command alone)env CAPTUREFAB_KEEP
capturefab preset apply bench -c sim:0 --dry-run
capturefab preset apply bench -c sim:0
capturefab preset apply --file bench.json -c sim:0 --strict
capturefab preset apply bench -c gige:00c0df123456 --persist UserSet1
capturefab preset apply JSON result

Sessions and jobs

Keep cameras open between commands and run captures and recordings in the background.

capturefab session

Sessions keep cameras open between commands: start one in the background, stop it, see it.

Camera commands keep their camera open in the auto session for 60s after their last use (--keep DUR to change it, --keep 0 or --no-session for none), and use a session that holds their camera on their own.

capturefab session start -c sim:0 --live
capturefab session status
capturefab session stop

capturefab session list

The running sessions. Effect: read.

capturefab --json session list
capturefab session list JSON result

sessions[{session,pid,uptime_s,cameras:[string]}]

jpeg{selected:auto|cpu|videotoolbox|nvjpeg|vaapi,backends:{libjpeg_turbo:{compiled,simd},videotoolbox|nvjpeg|vaapi:{compiled,available,verified?,reason?,version?,driver?,device?,integrated?,upload?:in-place|dma|copy}}} — the JPEG encoder CAPTUREFAB_JPEG selects; verified: the engine encoded a test frame as accurately as libjpeg-turbo, checked once a boot (a failure again after five minutes) and kept in the cache; nvjpeg and vaapi (Linux) run in a helper process; upload: how frames reach the GPU (read where the camera wrote them, one DMA, or written into its memory)
osstring
read_only_rootbool, absent off Linux or when it cannot tell — the root file system is mounted read-only
versionstring — Capturefab version
warm_sessionsbool — camera commands can keep their camera open in the auto session

capturefab shell

Run commands one after another with the cameras kept connected: a prompt in a terminal, one command a line otherwise. Effect: disruptive.

Commands are the ones above without capturefab. In a terminal: line editing, history, Tab completion, use CAM, cameras, show, help, exit; Ctrl-C stops the command running. Otherwise each line of stdin (or each -e) runs in order and prints one result, one JSON line each with --json; the first failure ends the run unless --keep-going, and sets the exit code.

capturefab shell arguments
Argument or optionMeaningValues
-c, --camera CAMCameras to connect now and keep connected, repeatable; the first is the camera of commands without -cenv CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA; repeatable
-e, --execute COMMANDRun COMMAND, then the next -e, instead of reading stdin; repeatablerepeatable
--keep-goingWithout a terminal: go on after a command fails; the exit code is then the first failure's—
--keep DURKeep the cameras open in a session for this long after the shell's last use (default 60s; 0 holds them in the shell's own process)env CAPTUREFAB_KEEP
capturefab shell -c sim:0
printf 'set exposure=5ms\ncapture -o a.png\ninspect\n' | capturefab shell -c sim:0 --json
capturefab shell -c sim:0 -e 'set gain=0' -e 'capture -o shot.png'
capturefab shell JSON result
FieldType and meaning
cameras{cameras:[{id,state:connecting|connected|failed,default?,session?,error?}]}
help{help} — the text of help COMMAND, or of a line's --help
linesinput: one command a line on stdin (blank and # lines skipped), or each -e; output: one line per command run, in order, its result or {error} as that command prints it (NDJSON with --json); the exit code is the first failure's
use{camera?} — the default camera
